Performance takeaways & Segmental Overview 
Deepak Group delivered its highest-ever quarterly and first-half performance in Q2 and H1 FY27, setting new benchmarks in revenue and profitability. 
Consolidated revenue reached ₹3,091 crore in Q2, registering 61% YoY growth, while EBITDA increased 187% YoY to ₹643 crore. For H1 FY27, revenue stood at 
₹5,682 crore, with EBITDA of ₹1,197 crore, reflecting growth of 48% and 173%, respectively.
The performance was achieved against a sharply volatile global operating environment, marked by geopolitical tensions, disrupted trade flows, feedstock 
constraints and elevated logistics costs. The Group successfully navigated these challenges while capitalising on emerging market opportunities, leveraging its 
integrated manufacturing capabilities, large domestic production base, operational flexibility and proactive commercial strategies. The growing preference for 
dependable local suppliers, particularly in import-dependent product categories, further reinforced the relevance of Deepak's manufacturing footprint and 
customer relationships.
Phenolics remained the principal growth and earnings driver, benefiting from a convergence of favourable market conditions, healthy operating throughput and 
effective supply-chain management. The business strengthened its position in the domestic market as disruptions to international supply chains increased the 
competitiveness of locally manufactured products. Meanwhile, Advanced Intermediates demonstrated commercial agility by recalibrating its approach towards 
volume-led growth, broadening customer engagement and recovering market share in select established product categories, even as competitive pricing and 
elevated operating costs persisted.
Importantly, the Group's performance also reflects the cumulative benefits of investments in manufacturing capabilities, backward integration, process efficiencies 
and energy optimisation. With newly commissioned assets progressively scaling up, new products moving through commercialisation and additional capacities 
approaching operational readiness, Deepak Group is strengthening its platform for diversified growth, greater downstream value addition and improved long-term 
competitiveness.

Segmental Overview 
Advanced Intermediates (AI) Phenolics
• The segment delivered 38% YoY revenue growth in Q2 FY27, supported 
by steady demand across established product lines, improved 
realisations in select categories and initial contributions from new 
products.
• In Q2, the business proactively prioritised higher volumes, customer 
acquisition and wallet-share recovery, successfully regaining market 
share across several basic intermediates.
• Segment Profitability was impacted by aggressive global pricing, 
elevated raw material and energy costs, higher export freight and 
deferred demand across certain agrochemical applications, partly offset 
by procurement efficiencies and integration benefits as well as cost 
benefits realized through backward integration initiatives. These costs 
are being passed on with some lag.
• The factors which are impacting the profitability of AI segment are 
contributing to enhanced competitiveness of phenolics segment. On a 
company wide basis, there is immense benefit.
• Buoyant outlook due to expected moderation in channel inventory 
destocking by customers, improving demand visibility, continued 
debottlenecking and the progressive commercialisation of specialty and 
downstream products provide avenues for higher volumes and an 
expanding product portfolio.
• Achieved the best-ever quarterly performance with Q2 revenue 
increasing 72% YoY to ₹2,291 crore and EBIT rising 256% YoY to ₹515 
crore. 
• Disruptions to imports, elevated international freight costs and tighter 
domestic product availability enhanced the competitiveness of our 
locally manufactured products.
• Proactive sourcing of inputs through diversification of suppliers and 
timely procurement interventions mitigated disruptions arising from 
geopolitical developments and constrained international supply chains.
• This enabled the company to ensure uninterrupted plant operations and 
full volume fulfillment thereby benefitting from firm realisations and 
healthy domestic spreads, which remained resilient as cost inflation 
across key feedstocks has been passed on.
• Advantageous market position expected to continue in forseeable 
future till it stabilises to new normal even as established market 
leadership, operating efficiencies and continued downstream portfolio 
expansion provide avenues for future growth.

CMD Message 
"The contours of global trade are being fundamentally reshaped by geopolitical tensions, disruptions to established supply chains and a 
growing emphasis on security of supply. Elevated freight costs, constraints in shipping availability and volatility in crude oil and 
petrochemical feedstocks are influencing sourcing decisions and competitive dynamics. At the same time, surplus capacities, particularly 
in China, and uneven demand across end-user industries continue to exert pressure on global chemical markets. In this evolving 
environment, competitiveness will increasingly be defined not merely by cost, but by quality, reliability and continuity of supply.
For India, these shifts present a significant opportunity. However, as we pursue Atmanirbhar Bharat, we must recognise that self-reliance 
must go hand in hand with global competitiveness. Our expanding domestic market, growing industrial capabilities and emerging trade 
partnerships provide a foundation for building chemical value chains benchmarked against the world's best in scale, technology, quality 
and reliability.
Against this demanding backdrop, Deepak Group has delivered record performance in Q2 and H1 FY27, reflecting the quality of our 
manufacturing assets, preparedness of our teams and operational agility. Our effort has been to maximize capacity utilization which has 
been achieved at all plants across the group. With this healthy utilization and proactive sourcing of critical feedstocks despite considerable 
supply-chain challenges, our Phenolics business was able to capitalise on favourable domestic market conditions and deliver an 
extraordinary performance. Conversely, export-oriented businesses within Advanced Intermediates faced competitive pressures and 
elevated logistics costs, which impacted margins despite volume gains. These contrasting dynamics demonstrate the advantages of our 
diversified portfolio and the ability to capture opportunities across different market cycles.
Our investments over the years have been guided by a long-term emphasis on world-class manufacturing, stronger integration and 
increasing value addition. We are now building upon this high-quality asset base through new specialty and agrochemical intermediates, 
downstream products and advanced materials, supported by research, innovation, energy efficiency and disciplined capital allocation. As a 
result, Deepak now enjoys scale and diversity with products ranging from commodity to specialties which unlock opportunities to improve 
performance as some segment of the business is well placed at all times.
An important cornerstone of this expansion is our integrated Propylene-to-Polycarbonate platform. With India's growing emphasis on 
electronics manufacturing, automobiles, electric mobility and other advanced applications, domestic demand for high-performance 
materials offers substantial long-term potential. We are progressing towards indigenous Polycarbonate Resin production, targeted towards 
the close of FY2030, creating an important opportunity for import substitution.
We remain committed to building a globally competitive Deepak Group that contributes meaningfully to India's industrial ambitions while 
creating enduring value for all stakeholders.”
Commenting on the performance for Q2 & H1 FY27 
Mr. Deepak C. Mehta (Chairman & Managing Director)
